body:
LandModel, EnergyHydrology, CanopyModel, SnowModel, SoilCO2Model and SlabLakeModel are now mutable structs. Every closure over a model (the tendency, cache update and diagnostic compute functions, the ClimaODEFunction, define_diagnostics!'s 103 closures) used to store a copy of the entire model struct inline, and since the struct's type embeds every parameter field and forcing input, compiling the construction of each closure cost seconds of pure codegen with no inference at all. With mutable structs the closures capture a pointer.

On my laptop, the global snowy land model this takes the compile time to the end of the first step from 307 s to 162 s: default_diagnostics from 62 s to 5 s, the ODE function construction from 23 s to 1 s, the LandSimulation constructor body from 25 s to 3 s and the time stepper's first step from 27 s to 6 s. 

On the clima cluster with a gpu, time drops from 560s to 450s. 

Over multiple benchmarks, I saw no change in runtime performance.

body:
Requires [SurfaceFluxes.jl#272](https://github.com/CliMA/SurfaceFluxes.jl/pull/272) (SurfaceFluxes 1.6).

- **Soil skin temperature solve**: Remove the post-solve bisection and flux-blending workaround in `solve_soil_surface_temperature_at_a_point`, as SurfaceFluxes 1.6 prevents surface-callback oscillations at low wind speed under buoyancy-dependent gustiness. Return `1` from `soil_evaporation_beta` when both `g_liq` and `g_h` vanish.
- **Soil surface phase from the top cell**: Decide once per skin solve whether the surface is frozen (`frozen_soil_surface`: the top cell contains ice and is below the depressed freezing temperature, the condition that already caps the skin temperature) and use that flag for the saturation humidity, latent heat, evaporation weight, the humidity callback, and the liquid/ice split of the vapor flux. The phase no longer switches with the skin temperature iterate, so the energy balance keeps a root when the skin cools through freezing over a thawing cell, where the previous choice from the iterate could leave it open by tens of W/m² at night; sublimation is booked only from ice that is present. A unit test covers the crossing on both sides of the freezing temperature.
- **Avoid unused surface-density and derivative evaluations**: Omit the flux temperature derivatives (`:∂lhf∂T`, `:∂shf∂T`) and the surface density extrapolation in `turbulent_fluxes_from_output` when neither derivative callback nor extra coupled fluxes are requested. `EnergyHydrology`, `SnowModel`, and `SlabLakeModel`, whose caches store no flux derivatives, return `nothing` from the derivative getters (the names are dropped from `snow_flux_names` and the lake flux type); the bucket keeps them because ClimaCoupler fills its cache directly with the full `flux_names` set. `compute_ρ_sfc` takes an optional `q_vap_sfc` and serves this path too. Reuse `p.soil.q_sfc` in `get_update_surface_humidity_function` instead of calling `component_specific_humidity` a second time.
- **Fuse canopy flux zeroing and deduplicate helpers**: Fuse `zero_canopy_fluxes_without_plants!` from 5–8 separate broadcasts into a single broadcast over `turbulent_fluxes` (a NaN vapor flux stays visible to the NaN check, as before); define `soil_flux_names` and `canopy_flux_names` for `boundary_var_types` and select the soil fields with them in `soil_turbulent_fluxes`; extract `snow_surface_humidity_and_derivative`; reuse `get_Vcmax25_leaf` in the Farquhar photosynthesis helpers and remove the unused `compute_J_leaf`/`compute_Jmax_leaf`.
- **Benchmarks**: Update the reference timings from benchmark build 3486: soil CPU 1.5 → 1.33 s, snowy land CPU 25.0 → 17.6 s and GPU 0.375 → 0.363 s. The soil GPU run was too noisy (σ ≈ mean) to move its reference.
title: Adopt SurfaceFluxes 1.6 and simplify surface-flux evaluations
